objective: Do patterns of knots hit the inherently sequential wall (P-completeness), and does the way their knots overlap predict when they do not? Known part, labelled: monotone circuits as atom patterns with every piece passing K1-K3; where not-all-equal and parity sit. New part: a knot-native measure of how atoms must be used as knots (untangling phases, rank), measured on random and structured atom patterns against native rounds, with one direction proved. Serves G3 and G16. Stop when the frozen predictions are read out, the proof is checked and the referee hand-off is made.
status: Complete 2026-11-16 (Successful; refereed SEQUENTIAL-WALL-R1, confirmed with fixes, no Block): forcing in atom patterns is P-complete (known) and order is forced only where an atom is used openly; phases of the forcing law are Strahler numbers (known). At the jump of random atom patterns rounds grow like n^0.30 to n^0.36 (312 at n = 2^20) and phases 0.57 per doubling (12); unlayered random circuits need at most 4 phases, layered ones about d^0.41; 34 knot laws placed (2 AC0, 2 parity-L, 14 P, 16 NP; none NL- or L-complete). Four wording corrections after the referee.
title: Which knot patterns must be worked in order
